name: Whey Protein
description: Fast-digesting milk-derived protein powder used to help meet daily protein needs, typically around workouts.
how_to_use: Mix 1 scoop (30g) with 250ml water or milk. Take 1–2 times daily, ideally post-workout or as a protein top-up between meals.
who_should_use: Adults who train regularly or want to increase daily protein intake and don't have a milk/dairy allergy.
age_recommendation: Not recommended for individuals under 18 without guidance from a doctor or dietitian.
precautions: Contains milk (dairy) and may contain soy/lecithin — check for allergens. Not a meal replacement. Consult a physician before use if pregnant, nursing, on medication, or managing a kidney/liver condition.

name: Mass Gainer
description: High-calorie protein + carbohydrate blend aimed at people trying to gain weight or muscle mass who struggle to eat enough through food alone.
how_to_use: Mix 2 scoops (60g) with 300ml milk or water. Take once or twice daily — ideally post-workout or between meals.
who_should_use: Adults with a high daily calorie/training demand (e.g. hard-gainers, strength athletes) under a calorie surplus goal.
age_recommendation: Not recommended for individuals under 18 without medical/dietitian supervision.
precautions: High in calories and sugar — not suitable for those managing blood sugar conditions (e.g. diabetes) without medical advice. Contains milk/dairy. Consult a physician before use if you have any pre-existing health condition.

name: Casein Protein
description: Slow-digesting milk protein, commonly used before bed to provide a steady release of amino acids overnight.
how_to_use: Mix 1 scoop (30g) with 250ml water or milk. Best taken 30 minutes before sleep.
who_should_use: Adults looking for sustained overnight protein release, without a dairy allergy.
age_recommendation: Not recommended for individuals under 18 without medical/dietitian supervision.
precautions: Contains milk (dairy). Not a meal replacement. Consult a physician before use if pregnant, nursing, or managing a kidney/liver condition.

name: Creatine Monohydrate
description: One of the most researched sports supplements; supports short-duration, high-intensity exercise performance and strength training output.
how_to_use: Take 3–5g daily mixed with water or a shake. Can be taken any time of day — consistency matters more than timing.
age_recommendation: Not recommended for individuals under 18 without medical supervision.
precautions: Drink adequate water through the day. Not recommended for people with pre-existing kidney disease without a doctor's approval. Consult a physician before use if pregnant, nursing, or on medication.

name: Pre-Workout
description: Blend typically combining caffeine and other performance ingredients (e.g. beta-alanine, citrulline) taken before training for energy and focus.
how_to_use: Mix 1 scoop with 200ml water and drink 20–30 minutes before your workout. Do not exceed 1 serving per day.
who_should_use: Healthy adults who tolerate caffeine well.
age_recommendation: Not recommended for individuals under 18, or anyone sensitive to caffeine/stimulants.
precautions: Contains caffeine/stimulants — do not combine with other caffeinated products, energy drinks, or take late in the day (may affect sleep). Avoid if you have a heart condition, high blood pressure, anxiety disorder, or are pregnant/nursing, without medical clearance.

name: BCAA
description: Branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine) commonly used to support muscle recovery, often consumed during or after training.
how_to_use: Mix 1 serving (10g) with 300ml water. Take during or immediately after your workout.
who_should_use: Adults training regularly, especially in a fasted state or on a calorie-restricted diet.
age_recommendation: Not recommended for individuals under 18 without medical/dietitian supervision.
precautions: Consult a physician before use if pregnant, nursing, or managing a metabolic condition (e.g. maple syrup urine disease, which specifically affects BCAA metabolism).

name: EAA
description: Essential amino acids — the full set of amino acids the body cannot produce on its own, used to support muscle protein synthesis and recovery.
how_to_use: Mix 1 serving (10g) with 300ml water. Take around your training session — intra-workout or post-workout.
who_should_use: Adults training regularly who want broader amino acid coverage than BCAAs alone.
age_recommendation: Not recommended for individuals under 18 without medical/dietitian supervision.
precautions: Consult a physician before use if pregnant, nursing, or managing a metabolic/kidney condition.

name: Glutamine
description: An amino acid commonly used to support recovery and gut/immune health, particularly during periods of intense training.
how_to_use: Mix 5g with water or a shake. Take post-workout or before bed.
age_recommendation: Not recommended for individuals under 18 without medical supervision.
precautions: Consult a physician before use if you have liver or kidney disease, or are pregnant/nursing.

name: Citrulline Malate
description: An amino-acid compound commonly used to support blood flow and reduce perceived fatigue during resistance training.
how_to_use: Mix 6–8g with water and take 30–60 minutes before your workout.
age_recommendation: Not recommended for individuals under 18 without medical supervision.
precautions: Consult a physician before use if you have low blood pressure, are on blood-pressure medication, or are pregnant/nursing.

name: Beta-Alanine
description: An amino acid used to buffer muscle acidity during high-intensity exercise; commonly causes a harmless tingling sensation (paresthesia).
how_to_use: Take 3–6g daily in split doses (e.g. 1.5–3g twice a day) to reduce tingling. Take consistently over 4+ weeks for the effect to build up.
who_should_use: Adults doing high-intensity interval or strength training.
age_recommendation: Not recommended for individuals under 18 without medical supervision.
precautions: Tingling/flushing sensation is common and not dangerous, but reduce dose if uncomfortable. Consult a physician before use if pregnant, nursing, or on medication.

name: Electrolytes
description: Mineral blend (typically sodium, potassium, magnesium) used to support hydration during long or sweaty training sessions.
how_to_use: Mix 1 sachet or 1 scoop with 500ml water. Drink during or after exercise, especially in heat or for sessions longer than 60 minutes.
who_should_use: Adults training in hot conditions, for long durations, or who sweat heavily.
age_recommendation: Generally suitable for most ages when following label serving size, but consult a doctor for children or anyone on a sodium-restricted diet.
precautions: Consult a physician before use if you have high blood pressure, kidney disease, or are on a medically prescribed sodium-restricted diet.

name: Multivitamins
description: Daily blend of essential vitamins and minerals used to help fill gaps in a regular diet.
how_to_use: Take 1 tablet daily with a meal. Do not exceed the labeled serving size.
who_should_use: Most healthy adults; especially useful for those with restrictive diets or high training volume.
age_recommendation: Formulated for adults — not for children unless a children's-specific product and doctor's guidance is used.
precautions: Do not exceed the labeled dose (excess fat-soluble vitamins can build up). Consult a physician before use if pregnant, nursing, or taking other vitamin/mineral supplements or medication.

name: Omega-3
description: Fish-oil (or algae-oil) derived essential fatty acids (EPA/DHA) commonly used to support heart and joint health.
how_to_use: Take 1–2 softgels daily with a meal.
who_should_use: Adults wanting to supplement dietary intake of omega-3 fatty acids.
age_recommendation: Formulated for adults unless a specific children's product is used.
precautions: May interact with blood-thinning medication — consult a physician before use if on such medication, pregnant, nursing, or allergic to fish/shellfish.

name: Vitamin D3
description: A fat-soluble vitamin that supports bone health and immune function, often supplemented due to low sun exposure.
how_to_use: Take 1 capsule daily with a meal, at the labeled dosage (typically 1000–2000 IU).
who_should_use: Adults with limited sun exposure or a known/suspected deficiency (ideally confirmed via a blood test).
age_recommendation: Formulated for adults unless a specific children's product/dose is used.
precautions: Do not exceed labeled dose — vitamin D can build up to harmful levels over time. Consult a physician before use if pregnant, nursing, or managing a calcium-related condition.

name: Magnesium
description: A mineral involved in muscle function, sleep, and recovery; commonly supplemented by athletes and people with disrupted sleep.
how_to_use: Take 1 capsule or tablet in the evening, daily. Best taken with a small meal.
who_should_use: Adults with high training loads or who want general recovery/sleep support.
age_recommendation: Formulated for adults unless a specific children's product/dose is used.
precautions: High doses can cause digestive upset. Consult a physician before use if you have kidney disease or are on medication (magnesium can interact with certain antibiotics and other drugs).

name: Zinc
description: A trace mineral supporting immune function and recovery, commonly paired with magnesium (ZMA-style blends).
how_to_use: Take 1 capsule or tablet daily with food.
age_recommendation: Formulated for adults unless a specific children's product/dose is used.
precautions: Do not exceed labeled dose — excess zinc can interfere with copper absorption long-term. Consult a physician before use if pregnant, nursing, or on medication.

name: Calcium
description: A mineral supporting bone density and muscle function, often paired with vitamin D3 for absorption.
how_to_use: Take 1–2 tablets daily with food, per label instructions.
who_should_use: Adults with lower dietary calcium intake (e.g. limited dairy consumption).
age_recommendation: Formulated for adults unless a specific children's product/dose is used.
precautions: Consult a physician before use if you have kidney stones, a thyroid/parathyroid condition, or take medication that interacts with calcium.

name: Protein Bars
description: Convenient snack-format protein bar for on-the-go protein intake.
how_to_use: Eat 1 bar as a snack or light protein boost between meals. Each bar provides approximately 20g of protein.
who_should_use: Anyone wanting a convenient higher-protein snack.
age_recommendation: Generally suitable for most ages as a snack food, but check the label for caffeine/stimulant-containing variants before giving to minors.
precautions: Check allergen panel (commonly contains milk, soy, nuts, gluten depending on flavor). Not a substitute for a balanced diet.
